translations.idiomatic: The other generals urged holding the city and waiting for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「彼遠來，未知我虛實，乘幕擊之，可挫其銳。

translations.literal: Wen said, "They have come from afar and do not know our strength or weakness; if we strike them while they are still in camp we can blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "They have come from far away and do not know our strength. If we strike them while they are still encamped we can blunt their momentum.

sentences.zh: 倘彼不退，固守未為晚也。

translations.literal: If they do not withdraw, holding firm will not yet be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not withdraw, it will not be too late to stand on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 」於是整兵出戰，元兵少卻。

translations.literal: " He then arrayed his troops and went out to battle; the Yuan army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: " He arrayed his troops and went out to fight. The Yuan forces gave ground.

sentences.zh: 已而圍城數重，溫斂兵固守，敵攻不能下，乃引去。

translations.literal: Before long they surrounded the city in several rings; Wen gathered his troops and held firm. The enemy attacked but could not take it and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy surrounded the city in several rings. Wen gathered his troops and held firm. The enemy could not take the city and eventually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱為奇功，擢大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: The Taizu called it a marvelous achievement and promoted him to Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu called this a remarkable achievement and promoted him to associate director of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 已，又命兼陝西行都督府僉事。

translations.literal: Later he was again ordered concurrently to serve as Associate Director of the Shaanxi Branch Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was later also appointed associate director of the Shaanxi branch military commission.

sentences.zh: 當蘭州之受圍也，元兵乘夜梯城而登。

translations.literal: When Lanzhou was besieged, Yuan troops scaled the walls by ladder at night and climbed up.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Lanzhou, Yuan troops scaled the walls by night.

sentences.zh: 千戶郭佑被酒臥，他將巡城者擊退之。

translations.literal: The Centurion Guo You, drunk, was asleep; another officer on patrol drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The centurion Guo You was drunk and asleep, but another officer on patrol drove them back.

sentences.zh: 圍既解，溫將斬佑，天策衛知事硃有聞爭曰：「當賊犯城時，將軍斬佑以令眾，軍法也。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, Wen was about to behead You; Zhu Youwen, administrative officer of the Tianche Guard, contended, saying, "When the bandits attacked the city, if the general had beheaded You to command the masses, that would have been military law.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was lifted, Wen was about to execute Guo You. Zhu Youwen, administrative officer of the Tianche Guard, objected: "When the enemy attacked the city, executing Guo You would have been proper military law.

sentences.zh: 賊既退，始追戮之，無及於事，且有擅殺名。

translations.literal: Now that the bandits have withdrawn, to pursue and kill him afterward serves no purpose in the affair and moreover bears the name of unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the enemy has withdrawn, killing him afterward serves no purpose and would be called unauthorized execution.

sentences.zh: 」溫謝曰：「非君，不聞是言。

translations.literal: " Wen apologized, saying, "But for you, I would not have heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: " Wen thanked him and said, "But for you I would never have heard this.

sentences.zh: 」遂杖佑釋之。

translations.literal: " He then had You beaten with the staff and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Guo You beaten with the staff and released him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而兩善焉，並賞有聞綺帛。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he approved both men and rewarded Youwen with patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he approved both men and rewarded Youwen with patterned silk.

sentences.zh: 其明年，以參將從傅友德伐蜀，功多。

translations.literal: The next year, as staff general he followed Fu Youde in the attack on Shu and achieved much merit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as staff general under Fu Youde in the campaign against Shu and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以副將會王弼等討西羌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, as vice-general he joined Wang Bi and others in suppressing the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served as vice-general with Wang Bi and others in the campaign against the western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 明年論功封會寧侯，祿二千石。

translations.literal: The next year, when merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huining with an income of two thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, for his merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huining with an income of 2,000 piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 又明年命往理河南軍務。

translations.literal: The year after that he was ordered to go oversee military affairs in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was ordered to oversee military affairs in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十四年從傅友德征雲南。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed Fu Youde in the campaign against Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he followed Fu Youde into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 二十年秋帥師討納哈出余眾，從北伐，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twentieth year he commanded troops to suppress the remnant followers of Naghachu and followed the northern campaign; in all he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twentieth year he led troops against the remnants of Naghachu's forces and took part in the northern campaign, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 後以居室器用僭上，獲罪，遂坐玉黨死。

translations.literal: Later because his residence and utensils exceeded what was proper for his rank he was found guilty and then executed by association with Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was found guilty of using a residence and furnishings that exceeded his rank, and was then executed as a member of Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 陳桓，濠人。

translations.literal: Chen Huan was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huan was a native of Hao.

sentences.zh: 從克滁、和。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Chu and He.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Chu and He.

sentences.zh: 渡江，克集慶先登。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he was first to ascend in the capture of Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing of the Yangzi he was first over the wall at the capture of Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 從取寧國、金華。

translations.literal: He followed in the taking of Ningguo and Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Ningguo and Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 戰龍江、彭蠡。

translations.literal: He fought at Longjiang and Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Longjiang and on Lake Poyang.

sentences.zh: 收淮東、浙西。

translations.literal: He recovered Huaidong and western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He secured Huaidong and western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 平中原。

translations.literal: He pacified the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 累功授都督僉事。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was appointed Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was appointed associate director of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年從伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he followed in the attack on Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu he took part in the campaign against Shu.

sentences.zh: 十四年從征雲南，與胡海、郭英帥兵五萬，由永寧趨烏撒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the campaign against Yunnan; together with Hu Hai and Guo Ying he commanded fifty thousand troops and advanced from Yongning toward Wusa.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he campaigned in Yunnan. Together with Hu Hai and Guo Ying he led fifty thousand troops from Yongning toward Wusa.

sentences.zh: 道險隘，自赤河進師，與烏撒諸蠻大戰，敗走之。

translations.literal: The route was perilous and narrow; advancing his army from the Red River, he fought a great battle with the barbarians of Wusa and routed them in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The route was perilous and narrow. Advancing from the Red River, he fought a major battle with the tribal peoples of Wusa and routed them.

sentences.zh: 再破芒部士酋，走元右丞實卜，遂城烏撒。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Mangbu tribal chief, drove off the Yuan Right Chancellor Shibu, and then walled Wusa.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the Mangbu tribal chief, drove off the Yuan right chancellor Shibu, and fortified Wusa.

sentences.zh: 降東川烏蒙諸蠻，進克大理。

translations.literal: He induced the surrender of the barbarians of Dongchuan and Wumeng and advanced to capture Dali.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the surrender of the tribal peoples of Dongchuan and Wumeng and advanced to capture Dali.

sentences.zh: 略定汝寧、靖寧諸州邑。

translations.literal: He pacified the prefectures and districts of Runing, Jingning, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the prefectures and districts of Runing, Jingning, and neighboring areas under control.

sentences.zh: 十七年封普定侯，祿二千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Puding with an income of two thousand five hundred piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Puding with an income of 2,500 piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 二十年同靖寧侯葉升征東川，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, together with the Marquis of Jingning Ye Sheng, he campaigned in Dongchuan and took very many captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he campaigned in Dongchuan with the Marquis of Jingning Ye Sheng and took a great many captives.

sentences.zh: 就令總制雲南諸軍。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to command all the armies of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then placed in overall command of the armies in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 再平九溪洞蠻，立營堡，屯田。

translations.literal: He again pacified the cave barbarians of Jiuxi, established fortified camps, and opened military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He again pacified the cave peoples of Jiuxi, established fortified posts, and opened military colonies.

sentences.zh: 還，坐玉黨死。

translations.literal: On his return he was executed by association with Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was executed as a member of Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 硃壽，未詳何許人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shou—it is not clear from where he came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shou's place of origin is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 以萬戶從渡江，下江東郡邑，進總管。

translations.literal: As commander of ten thousand households he followed in crossing the river, reduced the prefectures and districts of Jiangdong, and was advanced to Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of ten thousand households he followed the crossing of the Yangzi, secured the prefectures of Jiangdong, and was promoted to chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 收常、婺，克武昌。

translations.literal: He recovered Chang and Wu and captured Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He secured Chang and Wu and captured Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 平蘇、湖，轉戰南北。

translations.literal: He pacified Suzhou and Huzhou and fought back and forth north and south.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Suzhou and Huzhou and fought campaigns across north and south.

sentences.zh: 積功為橫海衛指揮，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became Commander of the Henghai Guard and was advanced to Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he became commander of the Henghai Guard and was promoted to associate director of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 與張赫督漕運，有功。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang He he supervised grain transport and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang He he supervised grain transport by water and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年封舳艫侯，祿二千石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Scullion with an income of two thousand piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Scullion with an income of 2,000 piculs of grain and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 坐玉黨死。

translations.literal: He was executed by association with Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed as a member of Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 曹興，一名興才，未詳何許人。

translations.literal: Cao Xing, also called Xingcai—it is not clear from where he came.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xing, also known as Xingcai, was a man whose place of origin is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 從平武昌，授指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Wuchang and was appointed Associate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Wuchang and was appointed associate commander.

sentences.zh: 取平江，進指揮使。

translations.literal: He took Pingjiang and was advanced to Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Pingjiang and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 克蘇九疇炭山寨。

translations.literal: He captured the Tanshan stockade of Su Jiuchou.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Tanshan stockade of Su Jiuchou.

sentences.zh: 進都督僉事，兼太原衛指揮。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission and concurrently Commander of the Taiyuan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate director of the chief military commission and concurrently commander of the Taiyuan Guard.

sentences.zh: 進山西行省參政，領衛事，為晉王相。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Administrative Commissioner of the Shanxi Branch Secretariat, took charge of guard affairs, and became Chancellor to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administrative commissioner of the Shanxi branch secretariat, took charge of guard affairs, and became chancellor to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，從沐英討洮州羌，降朵甘酋，擒三副使等。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu he followed Mu Ying in suppressing the Qiang of Taozhou, induced the surrender of the chief of Duogan, and captured the Third Vice-Commissioner and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Hongwu he followed Mu Ying in the campaign against the Qiang of Taozhou, accepted the surrender of the chief of Duogan, and captured the third vice-commissioner and others.

sentences.zh: 師還，封懷遠侯，世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaiyuan with hereditary succession as Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaiyuan with hereditary succession as commander.

sentences.zh: 理軍務山西，從北征有功。

translations.literal: He administered military affairs in Shanxi and followed the northern campaign with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He administered military affairs in Shanxi and distinguished himself in the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 後數年，坐玉黨死。

translations.literal: Several years later he was executed by association with Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was executed as a member of Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 同時以黨連坐者，都督則有黃輅、湯泉、馬俊、王誠、聶緯、王銘、許亮、謝熊、汪信、蕭用、楊春、張政、祝哲、陶文、茆鼎凡十余人，多玉部下偏裨。

translations.literal: At the same time those punished by association with the faction included, among regional commanders, Huang Yu, Tang Quan, Ma Jun, Wang Cheng, Nie Wei, Wang Ming, Xu Liang, Xie Xiong, Wang Xin, Xiao Yong, Yang Chun, Zhang Zheng, Zhu Zhe, Tao Wen, and Mao Ding—more than ten in all—most of them junior officers under Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Those punished at the same time by association with the faction included more than ten regional commanders: Huang Yu, Tang Quan, Ma Jun, Wang Cheng, Nie Wei, Wang Ming, Xu Liang, Xie Xiong, Wang Xin, Xiao Yong, Yang Chun, Zhang Zheng, Zhu Zhe, Tao Wen, and Mao Ding. Most had been junior officers under Yu.

sentences.zh: 於是勇力武健之士芟夷略盡，罕有存者。

translations.literal: Thus the brave and martially fit were mowed down almost entirely, and few survived.
translations.idiomatic: With this, the empire's bravest and most martial men were cut down almost to the last, and few survived.

sentences.zh: 謝成，濠人。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng was a native of Hao.

sentences.zh: 從克滁、和。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Chu and He.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Chu and He.

sentences.zh: 渡江，定集慶，授總管。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he secured Jiqing and was appointed Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing of the Yangzi he secured Jiqing and was appointed chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 克寧國、婺州，進管軍千戶。

translations.literal: He captured Ningguo and Wuzhou and was advanced to Centurion in charge of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ningguo and Wuzhou and was promoted to centurion in charge of troops.

sentences.zh: 戰鄱陽，平武昌，下蘇、湖，進指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He fought at Poyang, pacified Wuchang, took Suzhou and Huzhou, and was advanced to Associate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Lake Poyang, pacified Wuchang, took Suzhou and Huzhou, and was promoted to associate commander.

sentences.zh: 從大軍征中原，克元都，攻慶陽，搗定西。

translations.literal: He followed the great army in the campaign against the Central Plains, captured the Yuan capital, attacked Qingyang, and raided Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army in the campaign against the Central Plains, took the Yuan capital, attacked Qingyang, and raided Dingxi.

sentences.zh: 為都督僉事、晉王府相。

translations.literal: He became Associate Director of the Chief Military Commission and Chancellor to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He became associate director of the chief military commission and chancellor to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 從沐英征朵甘，降乞失迦，平洮州十八族。

translations.literal: He followed Mu Ying in the campaign against Duogan, induced the surrender of Qishijia, and pacified the Eighteen Clans of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Mu Ying in the campaign against Duogan, accepted the surrender of Qishijia, and pacified the eighteen clans of Taozhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武十二年封永平侯，祿二千石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongping with an income of two thousand piculs of grain and hereditary succession as Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongping with an income of 2,000 piculs of grain and hereditary succession as commander.

sentences.zh: 二十年同張溫追討納哈出余眾，召還。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, together with Zhang Wen, he pursued and suppressed the remnant followers of Naghachu and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he joined Zhang Wen in pursuing the remnants of Naghachu's forces and was then recalled.

sentences.zh: 二十七年坐事死，沒其田宅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was executed for an offense and his fields and residence were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was executed on a charge of misconduct, and his fields and residence were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 李新，濠州人。

translations.literal: Li Xin was a man of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin was a native of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，數立功。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river and achieved merit repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the crossing of the Yangzi and won merit again and again.

sentences.zh: 戰龍灣，授管軍副千戶。

translations.literal: He fought at Longwan and was appointed Deputy Centurion in charge of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Longwan and was appointed deputy centurion in charge of troops.

sentences.zh: 取江陵，進龍驤衛正千戶。

translations.literal: He took Jiangling and was advanced to Senior Centurion of the Longxiang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Jiangling and was promoted to senior centurion of the Longxiang Guard.

sentences.zh: 克平江，遷神武衛指揮僉事，調守茶陵衛，屢遷至中軍都督府僉事。

translations.literal: He captured Pingjiang, was transferred to Associate Commander of the Shenwu Guard, was posted to defend Chaling Guard, and through repeated transfers reached Associate Director of the Central Army Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Pingjiang, was transferred to associate commander of the Shenwu Guard, posted to defend Chaling Guard, and through successive promotions reached associate director of the central army military commission.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以營孝陵，封崇山侯，歲祿千五百石。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, for constructing the Xiaoling Mausoleum, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chongshan with an annual income of one thousand five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, for constructing the Xiaoling Mausoleum, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chongshan with an annual income of 1,500 piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 二十二年命改建帝王廟於雞鳴山。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to rebuild the Temple of Imperial Sovereigns on Jiming Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to rebuild the Temple of Imperial Sovereigns on Jiming Mountain.

sentences.zh: 新有心計，將作官吏視成畫而已。

translations.literal: Xin was resourceful in planning; the officials of the Directorate of Works merely regarded the completed drawings.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was shrewd and resourceful; the officials of the directorate of works merely carried out his finished plans.

sentences.zh: 明年遣還鄉，頒賜金帛田宅。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent back to his home district and bestowed gold, silk, fields, and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent home and granted gold, silk, fields, and a residence.

sentences.zh: 時諸勛貴稍僭肆，帝頗嫉之，以黨事緣坐者眾。

translations.literal: At that time the meritorious nobles gradually transgressed and acted wantonly; the emperor was quite jealous of this, and many were punished by association in factional cases.
translations.idiomatic: By then the meritorious nobles were growing increasingly extravagant and overbearing. The emperor resented this, and many were punished by association in factional cases.

sentences.zh: 新首建言：公、侯家人及儀從戶各有常數，余者宜歸有司。

translations.literal: Xin was the first to propose: the households of dukes' and marquises' families and their ceremonial attendants each have fixed numbers; the remainder should return to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was the first to propose that dukes and marquises be allowed only fixed numbers of household retainers and ceremonial attendants, with any excess returned to government control.

sentences.zh: 帝是之，悉發鳳陽隸籍為民，命禮部纂《稽制錄》，嚴公侯奢侈逾越之禁。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this, sent all those registered as dependents in Fengyang back to commoner status, ordered the Ministry of Rites to compile the Record of Regulations, and strictly forbade the luxury and transgressions of dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved. All dependent households registered in Fengyang were released to commoner status, the Ministry of Rites was ordered to compile the Record of Regulations, and strict prohibitions were placed on ducal and marquis extravagance.

sentences.zh: 於是武定侯英還佃戶輸稅，信國公和還儀從戶，曹國公景隆還莊田，皆自新發之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Marquis of Wuding Ying returned tenant households to pay taxes, the Duke of Xinguo He returned ceremonial attendants, and the Duke of Cao Guo Jinglong returned estate lands—all initiated by Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Marquis of Wuding Ying returned tenant households to the tax rolls, the Duke of Xinguo He returned ceremonial attendants, and the Duke of Cao Jinglong returned estate lands—all at Xin's instigation.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，督有司開胭脂河於溧水，西達大江，東通兩浙，以濟漕運。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he supervised the responsible offices in opening the Yanzhi River at Lishui, reaching the great river on the west and connecting to the two Zhe provinces on the east to aid grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he supervised the opening of the Yanzhi River at Lishui, linking it west to the Yangzi and east to the two Zhe provinces to aid grain transport.

sentences.zh: 河成，民甚便之。

translations.literal: When the river was completed the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal was completed the people found it a great convenience.

sentences.zh: 二十八年以事誅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was executed for an affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was executed on a charge of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：治天下不可以無法，而草昧之時法尚疏，承平之日法漸密，固事勢使然。

translations.literal: The commentator says: To govern the realm one cannot be without law, yet in the age of founding law was still loose, and in days of peace law gradually grew strict—this is indeed the natural tendency of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: A realm cannot be governed without law. In the founding age law was still loose; in days of peace it grew steadily stricter. That was simply the natural course of affairs.

sentences.zh: 論者每致慨於鳥盡弓藏，謂出於英主之猜謀，殊非通達治體之言也。

translations.literal: Discussants often sigh over the birds gone and the bow put away, saying it arose from the suspicions and schemes of an outstanding ruler—this is by no means language that comprehends the substance of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators often lament that when the birds are gone the bow is stored away, attributing this to the suspicions of a brilliant ruler. That is not language that truly grasps how government works.

sentences.zh: 夫當天下大定，勢如磐石之安，指麾萬里，奔走恐後，復何所疑忌而芟薙之不遺余力哉？

translations.literal: When the realm was greatly settled and secure as a bedrock, commanding ten thousand li and all rushing in fear of lagging behind—what suspicions remained that would require mowing them down without leaving any remainder?
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was fully settled, secure as bedrock, and commanders across ten thousand li hurried to obey, what suspicions remained that would require cutting them down to the last man?

sentences.zh: 亦以介胄之士桀驁難馴，乘其鋒銳，皆能豎尺寸於疆場。

translations.literal: It was also because men in armor were fierce and hard to tame; riding their sharp edge, all could raise some small measure of achievement on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: It was also because men in armor are fierce and hard to tame. At the height of their power, each could win some measure of glory on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 迨身處富貴，志滿氣溢，近之則以驕恣啟危機，遠之則以怨望扞文網。

translations.literal: When they came to dwell in wealth and honor, their ambitions full and their spirits overflowing—drawn near, arrogance and willfulness opened crises; kept distant, resentment and longing defied the written net of law.
translations.idiomatic: Once they dwelt in wealth and honor, their ambitions sated and their spirits overflowing, drawing close bred arrogance and crisis, while keeping them at a distance bred resentment and defiance of the law.

sentences.zh: 人主不能廢法而曲全之，亦出於不得已，而非以剪除為私計也。

translations.literal: The ruler could not abandon law to bend and preserve them completely; this too arose from having no alternative, and was not a private calculation to cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler could not set aside the law to preserve them intact. That too arose from necessity, not from a private desire to eliminate them.

sentences.zh: 亮祖以下諸人，既昧明哲保身之幾，又違制節謹度之道，駢首就僇，亦其自取焉爾。

translations.literal: The men from Liangzu downward, having failed to discern the subtle signs of preserving themselves wisely and having violated the way of observing regulations and careful measure, went to execution side by side—it was also what they brought upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From Liangzu downward, these men failed to read the signs that would have preserved them, violated the rules of restraint and proper measure, and went to execution together. They had brought it on themselves.
